domains.scope: Finite actual UInt64 binary64 patterns; canonical zero quotient only.

domains.scope: Exact dyadic/rational value of admitted finite binary64 patterns, tied to the pinned Lean unpack model; no decimal conversion or production arithmetic refinement.
coveredCriteria: Sign/exponent/fraction decomposition, normal hidden bit and subnormal exponent agree with the pinned Lean binary64 unpack model for every finite Number. Coefficient and exponent bounds, exact rational scaling, signed-zero equivalence and zero-normalization preservation are proved.

The universal model_nonfinite_rejected theorem rejects every exponent-2047 pattern, covering both infinities and every NaN; concrete admitted denotation witnesses cover signed minimum subnormals, minimum normal, signed one and maximum finite.
unmetCriteria: The raw-bit exact helper computes an unchecked field formula; only the finite Number wrapper is a semantic admission boundary. NumericInjectivity separately proves the converse from equal finite denotation to normalized-bit equality.

No complete decimal-to-binary64 nearest-even conversion, signed-zero/overflow/underflow endpoints, raw-integer conversion, shortest output, production NumberCodec instance or Bun/native refinement is supplied. RoundingInterval separately proves conditional sign-bit-zero interior midpoint cells. Pinned standard-library compiled imports remain trusted inputs.

domains.scope: Exact dyadic/rational denotation equality for every admitted finite binary64 value is equivalent to independently defined normalized-bit equality, including both signs and the signed-zero quotient.
coveredCriteria: Unbounded minimum-subnormal integer units strictly order exponent/fraction blocks and recover their fields; sign recovery identifies only the two zero patterns. Equal exact dyadic values are equivalent to equal normalized bits for finite Number inputs.
Exact rational equality has the same characterization. Denotation is injective on normalized finite numbers; signed zero is admitted as equivalent while distinct one and two are rejected.
unmetCriteria: The integer unit counts are unbounded mathematical values, not UInt64 accumulators; no machine range, allocation, time or stack refinement follows. Raw-field helpers remain synthetic outside the finite Number domain.

No decimal parser/printer, rounding selection, shortest rendering, production NumberCodec instance or Bun/native refinement is supplied. Pinned compiled standard-library imports and the Lean audit/kernel/runtime remain trusted.

domains.scope: Exact rational midpoint cells for finite sign-bit-zero interior values with two actual adjacent finite neighbors. Nonnegative means sign bit zero, including +0 and excluding -0; nearest comparisons quantify only over sign-bit-zero finite candidates.
coveredCriteria: Actual sign-bit-zero UInt64 code order agrees with exact rational order; consecutive finite codes have no intervening sign-bit-zero finite candidate. Rational midpoint inequalities exactly characterize closer-than and no-farther-than comparisons.

For an interior cell member, its center is no farther than every sign-bit-zero finite candidate; an odd center is strictly closer than every different such candidate. Cells include midpoint endpoints for even centers and exclude them for odd centers.

Coefficient parity equals the low bit of the binary64 code and matches the already-classified tie branch of pinned Lean Accuracy.roundToNearestEven. Concrete witnesses cover even/odd lower endpoints, asymmetric neighboring gaps around one, and equal gaps at the subnormal/normal boundary.
unmetCriteria: No interval theorem over negative candidates or -0, signed-zero center treatment, maximum-finite/overflow endpoints, universal rational-to-center selection or interval-coverage converse is supplied. Positive zero may be a predecessor, but the center must have both actual finite neighbors.

The tie result does not classify a residual or prove carry normalization/packing. There is no executable decimal-to-binary64 conversion, shortest coefficient/format choice, Ryu table/machine proof, production NumberCodec.Laws instance or Bun/native refinement.

Mathematical integers/rationals are unbounded. Input admission, digit/exponent bounds and stack/time/allocation/machine-width refinement remain separate. The exact subnormal boundary witness uses local kernel recursion/exponent reduction options without changing global tool resource limits.

domains.scope: Actual finite UInt64 sign reflection and exact rational symmetry; positive and reflected negative interior midpoint cells are nearest among every admitted finite candidate, including both signed zeros.
coveredCriteria: Sign toggling preserves finite exponent/fraction and parity, negates exact denotation, is injective and involutive. Signed zero bit patterns swap.
Interior nearest and odd strict-nearest results quantify all finite candidates; actual negative bit patterns are obtained by sign reflection with reversed neighbors.
unmetCriteria: Adjacency assumptions remain on the positive interior triple. No all-input selector or partition, decimal conversion, generic residual/carry/packing theorem, shortest renderer or production implementation refinement is provided.
Natural/rational intermediates are mathematical unbounded values. Machine, allocation and time refinement and trusted standard-library/kernel assumptions remain separate.

domains.scope: Exact signed zero/underflow and maximum-finite/overflow geometry over rational inputs and actual finite binary64 values, plus kernel-reduced signed dyadic round/pack witnesses. Infinity is a separate result refused by finite admission.
coveredCriteria: The closed zero cell is equivalent to zero being globally nearest among finite candidates; both zero patterns have equal distance and the selected zero sign is explicit. Actual minimum-subnormal adjacency and midpoint ties are proved.

Maximum finite has an actual predecessor and virtual next value 2^1024 excluded from the finite domain. Its proposed open finite cell has strict nearest distance; maximum being nearest among finite values itself has only a lower midpoint condition and remains true past overflow. Negative maximum nearest follows reflection.

BoundaryResult distinguishes finite values from signed overflow with matching finite admission/refusal. Concrete signed dyadic inputs below/at/above underflow and overflow invoke pinned Lean round and pack; exact rational inequalities establish their positions.
unmetCriteria: No total rational selector, complete partition or uniqueness theorem, generic all-input round/pack equivalence, decimal conversion or shortest rendering is proved. Endpoint point witnesses do not prove universal executable threshold behavior.

NegativeEndpoints separately proves negative maximum strictness and complete finite-nearest characterization, plus conditional reflected interior converses. Universal implementation correspondence remains open. A rational zero does not determine its sign; the model takes an explicit Sign.

Mathematical integer/rational arithmetic is unbounded; local kernel reduction options for large concrete witnesses do not prove machine-width, allocation, stack or time bounds. Standard-library imports and the proof/runtime trust assumptions remain.

domains.scope: Exact rational nearest and strict-nearest geometry over every admitted finite binary64 candidate, including sign reflection, negative maximum, both signed zeros, and conditional interior midpoint converses. Different bits define strict competitors; the two zero patterns are never strictly nearest.
coveredCriteria: Actual finite sign reflection preserves global nearest and strict-nearest predicates. Negative maximum is nearest exactly below or at its finite-neighbor midpoint and strictly nearest exactly below it; its finite cell is strict finite nearest combined with not negative overflow. Strictness quantifies over all finite candidates, not only a supplied neighbor.

For a nonnegative interior center with two supplied actual adjacent finite neighbors, global nearest is equivalent to the closed midpoint interval and strict nearest to the open interval. Both equivalences reflect to negative centers. The existing parity-based cell is equivalent to nearest for an even center and strict nearest for an odd center.

Concrete center, midpoint, distinct-neighbor, signed-zero and overflow witnesses expose the boundary distinctions. At negative overflow, negative maximum remains strictly closest among finite values, but the finite cell excludes the tie and the existing pinned round/pack witness is refused by finite admission.
unmetCriteria: Interior equivalences require their actual adjacency hypotheses; this module does not construct neighbors or a total selected center for every finite pattern/rational input, nor prove complete cell coverage or a global unique nearest-even selector. Signed-zero bit identity differs from rational denotation, so bitwise strict nearest is deliberately impossible for either zero.

Finite-nearest half-lines continue past overflow. Their characterization is not universal round/pack equivalence, decimal conversion, shortest rendering, a production NumberCodec.Laws instance or Bun/native refinement. The round/pack refusal is one concrete dyadic witness, not an all-input threshold theorem.

Mathematical integer/rational arithmetic is unbounded; machine width, allocation, stack and time bounds remain separate. Pinned compiled standard-library imports and the audit/kernel/runtime remain trusted.

unmetCriteria: No total rational rounding selector, cell coverage/uniqueness, decimal-to-binary64 conversion, shortest rendering, production NumberCodec instance or implementation refinement is supplied.
The absence of a nonnegative predecessor of positive zero does not assert the absence of a negative finite predecessor. Signed-zero policy and overflow remain separate endpoint obligations.

Phase09 full canonical JSON byte encoding/roundtrip/injectivity is not proved. JsonLayout proves recursive UTF-8 delimiter composition and unconditional canonical laws for number-free trees; results with numbers require NumberCodec.LawsOn. The numeric modules prove exact binary64/decimal denotations, finite denotation injectivity modulo signed zero, numeral grammar, all-sign interior midpoint minima, signed zero-cell characterization, complete negative-maximum finite-nearest/strict-nearest characterization, conditional all-sign interior midpoint converses, and finite endpoint geometry with concrete round/pack witnesses. FiniteNeighbors now constructs actual interior neighbors for every finite signed magnitude. Universal rounding selection/packing and complete numeric cell coverage remain open. No complete decimal-to-binary64 conversion or production number-codec instance, shortest rendering, full raw-document admission, or production refinement is supplied.
No production implementation is directly proved/refined by these theorems. Independent exact vectors and source/artifact bindings can provide sampled evidence, not a universal implementation theorem.
SchemaCheck and ByteSize are explicit semantic parameters; host cost sanity and exact integer/machine-width envelopes are explicit preconditions, not established production admission.

Lean standard-library imports are pinned/trusted compiled inputs; whole-import trust=0 rechecking is unqualified. Every authored theorem must undergo actual transitive axiom collection by the integrator.
Cryptographic collision resistance, host authority, physical filesystem behavior, external effects and liveness are outside this semantic core.
